adeliepenguin: An Adelie penguin standing upright, a medium penguin with a COMPLETELY BLACK HEAD, throat and back and a clean white front, and the one marking that identifies it: a NARROW CLEAN WHITE RING ENCIRCLES EACH EYE against the black face. Its bill is short and stubby and mostly hidden under black feathers, dull brick-red where it shows. Black flippers, pink feet.
chinstrappenguin: A chinstrap penguin standing upright, a medium penguin with a BRIGHT WHITE FACE, cheeks and throat, and the one marking that identifies it: a SINGLE FINE BLACK LINE RUNS UNDER ITS CHIN FROM EAR TO EAR like the strap of a helmet, with a black cap sitting above it. Black back and flippers, white front, black bill, pink feet.
gentoopenguin: A gentoo penguin standing upright, a tall penguin with a black head and the one marking that identifies it: a BROAD WHITE PATCH OVER THE TOP OF ITS HEAD JOINING ONE EYE TO THE OTHER ACROSS THE CROWN, like a white headband. Its bill is BRIGHT ORANGE-RED, its feet bright orange, its back blue-black and its front white.
kingpenguin: A king penguin standing tall and very upright, a large slender penguin with a smooth silver-grey back, a white front, and a BLACK HEAD carrying a LARGE TEARDROP-SHAPED BRIGHT ORANGE PATCH ON EACH SIDE, tapering downward and running into a soft golden-orange wash across its upper chest. Its bill is long, slim and slightly downcurved with an orange-pink stripe along the lower half.
antarcticicefish: An Antarctic icefish, a slender pale fish that is almost COLOURLESS AND FAINTLY TRANSLUCENT, its skin a bare scaleless greyish-white through which the pale pink shadow of the body shows. It has a large broad head with a wide flat mouth, LARGE DARK ROUND EYES, long delicate side fins held out like fans, and a slim tapering tail.
antarcticseaspider: A sea spider, a marine animal that is ALMOST ENTIRELY LEG: EIGHT VERY LONG THIN JOINTED LEGS spreading out wide like a drawing compass, meeting at a body so slender it is little more than a narrow rod between them. A short tubular snout projects forward from the front. Pale straw-yellow and semi-transparent. A marine animal, absolutely NOT a house spider and NOT a land arachnid.
antarctictoothfish: An Antarctic toothfish, a large heavy-bodied deep-water fish, mottled olive-brown and grey with darker blotches, a broad blunt head, a wide mouth, and LARGE PALE EYES SET HIGH ON THE HEAD. It has two separate fins along its back, one short and one long, and broad rounded side fins.
arcticchar: An Arctic char, a salmon-shaped fish with a streamlined body, a small adipose fin behind the main back fin, and a slightly forked tail. Its back is deep blue-green scattered with SMALL PALE PINK AND CREAM SPOTS, and its BELLY AND LOWER FINS ARE A BURNING ORANGE-RED, with the leading edge of each lower fin picked out in a clean white line.
arcticcod: An Arctic cod, a SMALL slender silvery-brown fish about the length of a hand, with a slightly projecting upper jaw, LARGE DARK EYES, a deeply forked tail, and A SINGLE SHORT WHISKER-LIKE BARBEL UNDER ITS CHIN. Three separate low fins run along its back and two along its underside.
capelin: A capelin, a SMALL slim silvery fish about the length of a finger, with a pointed head, a large mouth, a single small back fin set halfway along, a tiny adipose fin behind it, and a forked tail. Its back is olive-green and its flanks are brilliant mirror-silver with a fine dark line along them.
greenlandhalibut: A Greenland halibut, a large FLATFISH with a long oval body flattened side to side and held with one side facing the viewer, BOTH EYES ON THE SAME SIDE OF THE HEAD near a large upturned mouth. Unusually, it is DARK CHOCOLATE-BROWN ON BOTH SIDES rather than pale beneath, with long unbroken fins running the full length of the top and bottom edges.
colossalsquid: A colossal squid, an enormous heavy-bodied squid with a broad muscular reddish mantle, two large triangular fins at its rear, and EYES LARGER THAN DINNER PLATES, the biggest of any animal. Its eight arms and two longer tentacles carry ROWS OF SHARP SWIVELLING HOOKS as well as suckers, and its arms are thick and powerful rather than slender.
beardedseal: A bearded seal, a heavy grey seal with a small head on a very thick body, and the feature that names it: a DENSE MOUSTACHE OF LONG PALE WHISKERS spreading wide from its muzzle and CURLING INTO TIGHT SPIRALS AT THE TIPS when dry. Square foreflippers, a plain silvery-grey coat, and large dark eyes set close together.
hoodedseal: A hooded seal, a big silver-grey seal blotched with irregular black patches, with a broad muzzle. The adult male carries an INFLATABLE BLACK CUSHION OVER THE TOP OF ITS MUZZLE like a swollen hood between the eyes and nose, and can push a GLOSSY BRIGHT RED BALLOON OF MEMBRANE OUT OF ONE NOSTRIL, shown here half inflated to one side.
ringedseal: A ringed seal, a SMALL plump seal with a very short cat-like face, a small rounded head and large dark eyes. Its coat is dark grey-brown along the back and PATTERNED ALL OVER WITH PALE SILVER RINGS, each a light circle around a darker centre, fading to plain silver on the belly.
collaredlemming: A collared lemming in winter, a SMALL round-bodied rodent COMPLETELY PURE WHITE, with tiny ears buried in dense fur, a blunt rounded face, small black eyes, and a stub of a tail almost hidden. Its front paws carry TWO GREATLY ENLARGED FORKED DIGGING CLAWS on the middle toes, thick and pale like small chisels.
arcticwolf: An Arctic wolf standing, a wolf with a THICK CREAMY-WHITE COAT all over, noticeably SHORTER IN THE MUZZLE, EARS AND LEGS than other wolves and heavier through the chest and shoulder, so it reads as compact and stocky. Small rounded ears set low in deep fur, pale amber eyes, and a broad bushy tail.
rockptarmigan: A rock ptarmigan in winter, a plump ground bird with SNOW-WHITE PLUMAGE OVER ITS WHOLE BODY, a short stubby black bill, a NARROW BLACK STRIPE RUNNING FROM THE BILL THROUGH THE EYE, and a small SCARLET-RED FLESHY COMB above each eye. Its feet are FEATHERED RIGHT DOWN OVER THE TOES in white.
arctictern: An Arctic tern in flight, a slender silver-grey and white seabird with VERY LONG NARROW POINTED WINGS, a NEAT SOLID BLACK CAP covering the crown down to the eye, and a DEEPLY FORKED TAIL DRAWN OUT INTO TWO LONG FINE STREAMERS. Its bill is a slim pointed BLOOD-RED spike and its short legs are red.
ivorygull: An ivory gull, a compact gull ENTIRELY PURE WHITE from head to tail with no dark markings on the wings at all, standing on SHORT BLACK LEGS AND BLACK FEET. Its eye is a large dark bead, and its bill is short and slightly stout, blue-grey at the base grading to yellow with a pale tip.
rossgull: A Ross's gull, a SMALL delicate gull, pale pearl-grey above and white below with a soft ROSE-PINK FLUSH ACROSS ITS BREAST AND BELLY, a FINE COMPLETE BLACK RING AROUND ITS NECK like a thin collar, a very small black bill, and short red legs. Its tail is WEDGE-SHAPED, coming to a point in the middle.
snowpetrel: A snow petrel in flight, a SMALL seabird ENTIRELY PURE WHITE with no markings anywhere on its plumage, set off by a SHORT STOUT BLACK BILL, LARGE BLACK EYES, and small blue-grey feet. Its wings are broad and rounded at the tip and its tail short and slightly squared.
southpolarskua: A south polar skua, a heavy powerful gull-like seabird with a thick neck and a barrel chest, plumage plain cold grey-brown with a paler straw-coloured head and neck. Its bill is BLACK, HEAVY AND SHARPLY HOOKED AT THE TIP, and each wing carries a BOLD WHITE FLASH AT THE BASE OF THE PRIMARIES, showing as a bright patch near the wingtip.
littleauk: A little auk, a VERY SMALL dumpy seabird ABOUT THE SIZE OF A STARLING, almost neckless, with a black head, throat and back and a clean white belly. Its bill is TINY, STUBBY AND CONICAL, barely projecting from the face, and it stands upright on short legs set far back with small dark feet.
longtailedduck: A long-tailed duck drake, a small sea duck in bold pied black-brown and white, with a WHITE HEAD carrying a LARGE SMUDGED DARK CHEEK PATCH, a short bluish bill banded pink, and the feature that names it: TWO EXTREMELY LONG FINE BLACK TAIL FEATHERS trailing far behind the body, longer than the rest of the bird.
